long_biography.plain_text:
Austin Willis entered aviation through his own company, J.T. Power, after serving as a combat-dive-qualified engineer in the U.S. Army Special Forces. The business traded commercial jet-engine parts and leased aircraft, giving him direct experience in engine valuation and aftermarket supply. He sold most of its assets and operations to Willis Aeronautical Services, then joined Willis Lease Finance in corporate development. His path into the family-founded group therefore paired separately built operating experience with an established family platform.

Willis became chief executive in 2022, succeeding his father, Charles F. Willis IV, who remained executive chairman. He leads an integrated business spanning aircraft-engine leasing, parts, maintenance, asset management and structured finance. Under his tenure, the company has expanded institutional partnerships and its third-party asset-management capabilities while continuing to invest in engine assets. The role combines operating responsibility with a substantial ownership interest in the family-controlled group.

uncertainties: The exact identity is conclusive. The upstream biography already names WLFC, Charles F. Willis IV and Austin's chief-executive role, while SEC, company and Companies House records match those details and independently bridge Fabulous Character's holding company to WLFC.

The vessel is legally registered to Willis Lease Marine LLC, not to Austin Willis personally. Current SEC schedules show WLFC holds a 65% membership interest in that entity. The yacht association is therefore a corporate and controlling-family anchor, not proof that Austin alone is the beneficial owner.

Wealth origin is Mixed because the public record documents three material mechanisms: Willis founded and sold J.T. Power, owns WLFC shares directly and through compensation, and holds an interest in a family partnership that owns father-founded WLFC stock. The filings do not disclose whether the partnership interest was purchased, gifted or otherwise transferred.

Operator is selected because Willis currently runs WLFC as chief executive and materially directs strategy and capital allocation. He did not found WLFC, so Founder would wrongly substitute the earlier J.T. Power venture for the principal current wealth platform.

Aviation & Aerospace is used for both wealth-creation and primary industry because both J.T. Power and WLFC centre on commercial aircraft engines, leasing, parts and services. Structured finance is instrumental to the aviation platform rather than a separate primary sector.

The active tag set is limited to Aviation. Aerospace is adjacent, but the evidence centres on commercial aircraft operation, engine leasing and aftermarket services rather than aerospace manufacturing or space systems.
Companies House supplies only June 1980, while the SEC provides age 45 as of April 2026. The birth month and year are proposed, but the exact day and place of birth remain unproposed.

No secondary nationality or secondary residence was established. No authenticated personal LinkedIn, Instagram or website was found, and no dedicated Forbes profile exists; only the official WLFC biography is proposed.

The existing upstream biography is accurate in broad corporate terms but is vessel-dependent and discusses the father more than the assigned person. A durable personal biography is therefore proposed as a correction.
